name: adplay
why: Plays AdLib OPL2 chip music from the 1990s DOS era in the terminal, a real trip into how old sound cards worked.

brief.what_it_is: AdPlay/UNIX is a console-based player for AdLib and Sound Blaster OPL2 music files, the UNIX frontend of the AdPlug project. You start it with one or more music files as parameters, and it plays them through the terminal. AdPlug's core library reads a large number of old game and tracker music formats (the homepage lists over 60, including A2M, CMF, D00, RAD, S3M and ROL) and renders them with an emulated OPL2 chip. The homepage notes that the library can also drive real hardware, but the UNIX player's README says only emulated OPL2 output is supported.
brief.why_it_exists: AdPlug's homepage describes it as a free, cross-platform, hardware independent AdLib sound player library that plays sound data 'directly from its original format' so that no OPL chip is required for playback. AdPlay/UNIX is the stand-alone console front end built on that library.
brief.how_it_works: AdPlug has a separate replayer for each supported file format, so each game or tracker format is interpreted on its own terms instead of being converted to MIDI or WAV first. The OPL2 register writes are then sent to an emulator, and AdPlay/UNIX lets you pick among output devices, per its README. The README says only emulated OPL2 output is supported in the UNIX player.

brief.install_notes: Homebrew installs the adplay executable. For building from source, the README requires the AdPlug library version 1.4 or newer, or 2.2 or newer for full feature support. A git checkout also needs autoconf, automake and libtool to generate the configure script. No accounts, runtimes or first-run configuration are mentioned. The README says to start the player with at least one file as a parameter.
brief.standout: It plays the original music of 1990s DOS games and trackers from their native file formats instead of converting them, and the OPL2 chip is emulated in software so no sound card is needed. Its format list is far wider than most players of this kind.
brief.status: Maintained. The homepage lists AdPlay/UNIX 1.9 released 2025-12-21 and AdPlug core 2.4 released 2025-04-06, with a note that 1.9 added SDL2 compilation support and a RAW file writer. I did not check commit dates on the repository.
brief.caveats: The README says the documentation is thin: 'A more detailed doc will follow when i get the time to write one.' Playback is emulated OPL2 only, according to the README. Building from source needs the separate AdPlug library and an autotools toolchain. The homepage copyright line reads 2001 - 2015 while the README reads 2001 - 2025, which I did not try to resolve. I did not find a licence statement in the AdPlay/UNIX README itself; the homepage says AdPlug is released under the LGPL.
